description: Fresh ordinary-language retrieval evaluation, development: 30 turns in 10 related scenario families. No section numbers in user prompts. Source keys do not enter normal retrieval/writer.

scope.zoningTextThrough: 2026-08-13; source version, not proof of all later amendments
scope.grading: Assistant-authored and source-reviewed, not professionally adjudicated; correlated follow-ups are reported by family.

questions: For a new NYC office under the 2022 codes, does a required exit door with a 31-inch clear opening meet the ordinary minimum width? There is no special door exception and its occupant load does not require a larger opening.
If I use two 30-inch-clear leaves without a center mullion, can I add their widths together to satisfy that minimum?
When checking a swinging door, do I measure with it open at 90 degrees or use the nominal leaf width?
checks: No. Ordinary required minimum clear opening is 32 inches, subject to occupant-load capacity. Clear opening is not nominal door-leaf width.
No. Where the 32-inch minimum applies, at least one leaf of a pair without a mullion must provide a 32-inch clear opening.
Measure the clear opening between the face of the door and the stop with the door open 90 degrees; nominal leaf width alone is not the clear opening.

questions: For an ordinary straight office stair in a new NYC building under the 2022 codes, are 7.5-inch risers acceptable? This is not a dwelling, spiral stair, or assembly aisle.
I will reduce the risers to 7 inches. Can the rectangular treads be 10 inches deep?
In that same flight, the smallest riser is 6 inches and the largest is 6.5 inches. Is that variation acceptable?
checks: No. Ordinary riser maximum is 7 inches and minimum 4 inches.
No. Rectangular tread depth is at least 11 inches measured horizontally between foremost projections of adjacent treads.
No. The half-inch variation exceeds the 3/8-inch maximum variation in a flight. No stated exception applies.

questions: For a new NYC office under the 2022 codes, may washbasins be supplied with tempered water instead of hot water? I am asking about the required type of supply, not its exact temperature.
What about a nonresidential laundry in the same project: would only cold water satisfy the supply rule?
Where a fixture has a maximum permitted delivery temperature, can the water-heater thermostat alone serve as its required temperature-limiting means?
checks: Yes. Nonresidential bathing and washing purposes may be supplied with hot or tempered water.
No. Nonresidential laundry purposes require hot water.
No. A water-heater thermostat must not serve as the code-required temperature-limiting means for maximum hot or tempered delivery temperatures at fixtures.

questions: For a new NYC building under the 2022 codes, can an open plumbing vent terminate 18 inches above a roof used only for maintenance?
If that roof becomes an occupied observation deck, what height above the roof is required for the open vent?
For the roof extension, can a 3-inch vent continue unchanged through the roof? Where would an increase to the required size have to occur?
checks: No. Open vent termination through an ordinary roof is at least 24 inches above the roof.
At least 7 feet above the roof for an assembly, promenade, observation, sunbathing or similar occupied roof.
No. Roof or wall vent extension must be at least 4 inches diameter; increase must occur at least 1 foot inside the thermal envelope.

questions: In a new NYC office under the 2022 codes, can ordinary mechanical exhaust air be discharged into the attic instead of outside? This is not a whole-house attic fan or a listed ductless cooking hood.
If we move that exhaust outside right beside the fresh-air intake, does reaching the exterior alone satisfy the rule?

For a separate residential kitchen, is a listed and labeled ductless range hood always required to discharge outdoors? Assume it is installed to the manufacturer instructions and the kitchen otherwise has the required ventilation.
checks: No. Ordinary mechanical exhaust discharges outdoors; air must not be exhausted into an attic or crawl space. Stated exceptions do not apply.
No. Exhaust discharge must not cause a nuisance and must be located so it cannot readily be drawn back in by a ventilating system; outlet distance provisions also apply.

No. The stated listed/labeled domestic ductless range-hood exception allows no outdoor discharge when manufacturer instructions and other required mechanical or natural ventilation are satisfied. This is not a blanket exemption for all exhaust systems.

questions: In a commercial NYC vehicle service area under the 2022 codes, gasoline engines are run while vehicles remain stationary for diagnostics. Is general room ventilation enough, or is tailpipe capture also required?
If the service area operates and repairs only electric vehicles, does that same tailpipe-capture section apply?
What if gasoline engines are run indoors only long enough to move vehicles in and out, with all diagnostics done outside?
checks: Source capture directly connected to motor-vehicle exhaust systems is additionally required, alongside mechanical ventilation. Capture must be engineered by a registered design professional or factory-built and designed/sized for the purpose.
No. That section expressly does not apply to vehicles operated or repaired that are electrically powered. Do not claim exemption from every other ventilation requirement.
The service-area exception to this section applies when engines operate inside only for movement into and out of the building; do not claim no other ventilation rules apply.

questions: For a gas-fired boiler in a new NYC building under the 2022 codes, is a sediment trap required if the boiler has none built into it?
Should that trap be upstream or downstream of the appliance shutoff valve?
Would the same external-trap requirement apply to an ordinary gas range with no built-in sediment trap?
checks: Yes. A sediment trap is required where not incorporated in the appliance, unless a named exempt appliance applies; ordinary boiler is not listed as exempt.
Downstream of the appliance shutoff valve, as close to appliance inlet as practical.
No. Ranges are expressly among appliances that need not be equipped with the sediment trap under this provision. Do not turn the boiler answer into a universal requirement.

questions: In a new NYC building under the 2022 codes, may fuel-gas piping run through an ordinary HVAC return-air duct?
Could we move it into a shaft that contains a fire standpipe riser instead?
What about using the fire-pump room as the access route into a gas-meter room?
checks: No. Gas piping must not be installed in or through supply, return or exhaust ducts.
No. Gas piping must not be installed in any shaft containing standpipe risers.
No. Access to gas-meter rooms must not pass through spaces housing a fire pump. Gas piping, appliances and other gas equipment are also prohibited within such spaces.

questions: In NYC, may students keep and use ordinary wax candles in a Group R-1 college dormitory?
For a separate ordinary office where candle use is otherwise allowed, how far must a lit candle be kept from curtains or other combustible materials?
If the holder is secured and on a noncombustible surface, may the person attending that office candle leave while it is still lit?
checks: No. Storage or use of candles, incense and similar open-flame producing items is prohibited in Group R-1 college and university dormitories.
At least 3 feet from combustible material or combustible waste; other safety precautions remain applicable.
No. Candles and other unenclosed open flames must be constantly attended while lit; placement precautions do not waive attendance.

questions: For a permanent open accessory parking facility in a NYC C4-2 commercial district, can we leave the surface as dusty bare soil?
Would permeable paving be allowed, or must the surface be conventional asphalt?
If the paving is dustless but the site is graded so water collects without adequate drainage, is the surfacing rule satisfied?
checks: No. Grading, construction, surfacing and maintenance must provide adequate drainage and prevent dust. Permanent open accessory group parking requires permeable paving, asphaltic or Portland cement concrete, or another hard-surfaced dustless material.
Permeable paving is expressly allowed; conventional asphalt is not mandatory. Adequate drainage and dust prevention still apply.
No. Adequate drainage is required as well as dust prevention; one does not substitute for the other.
